#2696. Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram

In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings.

Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and "the Jazz."

Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that.

We're about to find out if they belong on such a list.

Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone's list.

Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always.

Morant doesn't particularly address any of those, and yet, he's here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson.

Heck, the Blazers' most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit," General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday.

The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team's annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It's happening.

"It's easy for people to be like, 'Man how is this going to work,'" Lillard offered. "'They can't do this, they can't do that.' But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that."

The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn't the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be.

Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary.

But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn't uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come.

That's what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We're going to need to see it to believe it.

Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That's how basketball works.

"That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be," Morant said.

The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense.

"It's about being a complete basketball player for myself," he said, "and I think we have a lot of guys like that."

There is a long history of teams talking themselves into superstar additions that make little sense. The Los Angeles Lakers once made a conscious decision to acquire Russell Westbrook and pair him with LeBron James. Nobody made them do that!

The talent and star power of a Lillard-Morant backcourt is undeniable. Still, I remain unconvinced that Cronin, with a very hands-on new owner in his ear, made the deal with winning basketball games at the front of mind.

Although, admittedly, Cronin's biggest wins as a GM have been in the trade market.

The haul of assets he collected for Lillard, only to get him back two years later, will go down as an all-time great swindle. So, too, will the oft-questioned Avdija trade a year later.

Maybe he sees something in a Lillard-Morant pairing that many of us can't.

Morant could return to the All-Star form he had achieved before injuries and off-court issues derailed his ascent. And if he does, the Blazers can either trade him for pieces that fit better or clear out the logjam and build around him.

But to sell the current roster as a basketball strategy doesn't quite pass the smell test.

Neither Lillard nor Morant has achieved stardom due to his defensive acumen. Each player needs the ball in his hands to thrive. If the duo is on the floor together, Avdija is no longer the secondary playmaker, he becomes tertiary.

So, you are left to wonder whether the Blazers sold themselves on Morant because of how he can help the current collection of talent or if they simply saw the opportunity to land a 27-year-old All-NBA talent for cheap, regardless of what it meant for the existing roster construction.

And if you're being honest, you probably don't need to wonder which of the two it is.

"We were very focused and we'll continue to be on … adding to our talent base as much as we can," Cronin said.

That thinking right there may tell you just how far ahead of everyone else the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are in the Western Conference. They are positioned to dominate for the next half-decade, if not longer. The only chance any other team has of disrupting that is taking bold risks.

But I thought the goal was to go all in on the twilight years of Lillard's career?

"Dame literally just wants to win," said first-year head coach Micah Nori, whose charge is to sort out arguably the most talented glut of point guard talent in NBA history. "I think that's the only thing left he really has to (do). He's already proven he's a winner, but at the highest level."

Does adding Morant move Lillard closer to a title? Or simply give Portland a potential off-ramp if Lillard is no longer the same player after tearing his Achilles tendon?

Morant was without question a low-risk, high-reward addition. He came at the reasonable price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. If it becomes clear that Morant is one point guard too many, or that he's just not the player he once was, some will argue that it didn't cost the Blazers much to try.

However, there is an opportunity cost to messing with Lillard's swan song. If you don't get it right, you risk wasting the gift of his voluntary return last summer. And, not for nothing, Lillard has the option to become a free agent again after this season.

The franchise icon certainly hasn't said anything that would suggest he is unhappy about Morant's presence, although he stopped short on Monday of a full-throated endorsement. He said he knew about the trade before it went through.

When I asked if he thought it was a good idea right away or if he needed time to get on board with the plan, Lillard said, "My position on it was, I'm prepared for whatever."

It's good that he's already thinking about other positions. Because his old one is getting awfully crowded.

#2695. Fernando Mendoza gets 3-word message from Kirk Cousins after Raiders trade

Fernandomania has officially begun in the desert.

With the Las Vegas Raiders trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings in before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Las Vegas are expected to turn to Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in the draft earlier this year, under center.

Mendoza is slated to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks at home on Sunday, Nov. 15 (4:05 ET).

Mendoza's lone regular-season action came during his debut, at the end of a Week 4 road loss to the New England Patriots on Oct. 11. He finished 6-for-8 passing for 48 yards.

Mendoza's first two opponents boast vaunted defensive units. Seattle's defense, dubbed the "Dark Side" for a reason, did not allow a touchdown last week to the undermanned Arizona Cardinals. Looking ahead, the Raiders face the Denver Broncos on the road in Week 11. Denver ranks in the top 10 in points allowed per game (20.7), sacks (26) and takeaways (12).

"I feel that Fernando has done a great job," Cousins told reporters Oct. 26. "He has a bright future ahead. I'm going to try and go out there and play as well as I possibly can and try and win and give him a good example to learn from."

On his Instagram story, Cousins offered a goodbye to "Raider Nation" and a message to Mendoza, whom Cousins tagged in the post.

Toughening matters for Mendoza on the field will be the lack of a rushing attack for the Raiders. First-round talent Ashton Jeanty from the 2025 draft has not worked out, although rookie Mike Washington has shown some juice in the backfield. Still, Las Vegas ranks 31st in rushing yards per game (71.3) and is last in yards per rush (2.9).

Similar to Cousins, Mendoza will likely have to shoulder much of the output in the Raiders' offense.

"The game has to be balanced," head coach Klint Kubiak said following the team's most recent loss to the San Francisco 49ers that dropped their record to 4-5. "You can't be a running and throwing team when you're throwing it every time. That's not easy.

"You got to start the game a lot faster. You got to go toe-to-toe in the first half so that the second half isn't a throwing fest."

The good news is that tight end Brock Bowers ranks ninth in the league in receiving yards and provides a crucial red-zone target with six touchdowns already this season. Wide receiver Tre Tucker emerged as a reliable downfield option for Cousins, which gives Mendoza more relief in the passing game.

#2694. ‘Thank goodness he’s on our team’: Cooper Flagg makes history, Dallas Mavericks keep stacking wins

With the Dallas Mavericks down 13 points late in the first half on the second night of a back-to-back, Monday night at American Airlines Center looked very much like a schedule loss. Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving had other ideas, though, as they combined for 78 points, fueling Dallas past the Indiana Pacers in a wild finish, 125-122.

The win was the Mavericks' third straight and moved Dallas to 7-4 on the season. It also put the Mavs three games over .500 for the first time since March 1, 2025, a date that feels a lot longer ago than it actually is for anyone who has lived through the last two years of Mavericks basketball.

Think about where this franchise was not long ago. The Luka Doncic trade. Irving's torn ACL. A 26-56 season and back-to-back years without a playoff appearance. Oddsmakers set Dallas' win total at 34.5 before this season, and after an opening stretch that included Houston, San Antonio and Oklahoma City, a lot of people expected the Mavs to be scrapping just to stay afloat by mid-November.

Instead, the Mavs are stacking wins, Flagg looks like an MVP candidate in year two, and Irving looks like his old self before the ACL injury happened. Most importantly, the way the Mavs are winning these games feels sustainable. Here are some of the biggest storylines from Monday night's thriller.

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks dunks during the first half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Flagg was good in the first half, but he was on an entirely different level in the second.

The 19-year-old star scored 30 of his season-high 43 points after halftime, including 14 on 6-of-6 shooting in the third quarter and 16 more in the fourth. He finished 16-of-25 from the field, 3-of-6 from 3-point range and a perfect 8-of-8 at the free-throw line, adding 10 rebounds, six assists, three steals and a block for his fourth straight double-double.

Flagg became just the second teenager in NBA history to post at least 40 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a game, joining Kevin Durant, who put up 42 points, 13 rebounds and six assists in the final game of his rookie season with Seattle in 2008. Per StatMuse, add the three steals, and Flagg is the first teenager ever with a 40-10-5-3 line.

It was also his fifth career 40-point game, as many as the next two teenagers on that list combined (LeBron James with three and Anthony Edwards with two). His 14th career 30-point game moved him into second place for the most by a player under 20, behind only James, and his seventh 35-point game tied James for the most by a teenager. And keep in mind, Flagg doesn't turn 20 until Dec. 21.

Mavericks head coach Dusty May pointed to how complete Flagg's scoring package has become.

"He gets to the rim," May said in his postgame media availability. "I think him almost being a left-handed player in the paint certainly helps. He's a great left-footed jumper, left-handed finisher. Then he's able to square in the air from 15, 17 feet. … The last couple of games, he's made some threes and he's making all of his free throws. That's how you put up the 43 points, where you do a little bit of everything."

It's almost unreal just how good Flagg already is, and May is just happy he's on his roster and not having to gameplan against him.

"He affects the game in so many ways and he makes the right plays as far as passing," May said. "Thank goodness he's on our team. It's unbelievable that he's a 19-year-old doing this."

Flagg's deadly midrange shot, which he worked on all offseason, is paying off in a big way, especially in clutch situations, where he leads the league in clutch points.

"I think just being able to get to my spots at a higher level and being more comfortable with that has allowed me to take a little bit of load off my body," Flagg said. "Just kind of stopping short, raising up over people. It's taxing going downhill all the way to the rim and trying to finish over seven-footers all night, every night. … Just trusting the work, trusting the spot work that I put in all summer long."

Through 11 games, the reigning Rookie of the Year is averaging 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 2.2 steals per game. Again, given everything Mavs fans have been through over the last 21 months, this sort of euphoric rise back to genuine happiness watching these games is hard to believe.

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Kyrie Irving #11 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates after scoring a three point basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Flagg was the closer on Monday night, but Irving was arguably the reason Dallas was still in the game in those closing moments.

Playing the second night of a back-to-back for the first time this season, a day after logging 28 minutes in a 130-93 win over Brooklyn, Irving poured in 35 points in a season-high 38 minutes. He knocked down a season-high seven 3-pointers on 10 attempts, went 3-of-3 at the line and finished a game-best plus-29.

After missing 19 months with the torn ACL he suffered in March 2025, Irving said he told his teammates in the locker room after Sunday's win that he planned to play.

"When you're in a combative sport such as basketball, some days are going to feel good, some days aren't, especially coming off an injury or a long period of time," Irving said. "So I just had to get my body back used to being in the flow of the game. … I was just feeling great, and just coming in to today."

May, who said plus-minus is often overblown in a one-game sample, made an exception for Irving in this one.

"His plus-29 tonight was very indicative of how important he is," May said. "When we were struggling to make shots in the first half, we thought we were generating really good looks. We just looked a little bit flat. I thought Kyrie's shot-making just kind of righted the ship for us."

It's still early, but seeing Irving look this healthy and proving to be a seamless fit next to Flagg bodes well for what this team can accomplish this year. Perhaps the last two years of the basketball injury gods punishing the Mavs will result in some good injury luck the rest of this season.

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates with teammate Kyrie Irving #11 of the Dallas Mavericks after scoring a basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The most encouraging part of all of this is just how naturally Flagg and Irving shared the scoring load against Indiana. The two combined for 26 fourth-quarter points, including Dallas' first 13 of the period, and May said neither player blinks when the play call goes to the other.

"We're coming out of a timeout, we may draw up a play for one of them just because the other one might have an All-League defender on him, or whatever the case, and they never roll their eyes," May said. "They know when we're going to one of the two, the other one's very, very supportive because they have that much respect for each other."

Irving, an established champion who has shared the floor with more than a few superstars over his 15-year career, is grateful that he's able to be Flagg's teammate, despite the two players being on different ends of their careers.

"We keep calling him a teenager, but he plays way beyond his years. We've got to give him his flowers," Irving said. "Most young guys will probably move away from that contact, but it seems like this newer generation that's coming into our league, they fear nothing. And I think he falls right in line with that. So grateful to have him on the wing with me."

Those feelings are mutual for Flagg: "Just having [Kyrie] out there, his gravity opening the floor for everybody else, it makes my life so much easier."

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: P.J. Washington #25 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates a three point basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

It wasn't pretty at the end, but it didn't have to be for the Mavs to come up with another win. That's one thing that's been so encouraging about this fast start to the season. Dallas is finding different ways to win, whether it's pretty or not.

Indiana's Pascal Siakam torched Dallas for 26 first-half points on 8-of-9 shooting, but the Mavs adjusted their help defense after the break and held him to just three points on 1-of-7 shooting the rest of the way. The Pacers took a 66-56 lead into halftime and a 93-90 lead into the fourth before Flagg buried a 26-foot pull-up 3 to tie it. Irving's 23-footer with 9:36 left put Dallas in front for good.

Leading 125-122 with a chance to put the game on ice, PJ Washington missed a pair of free throws with four seconds left, and Caleb Martin bailed everyone out by stealing Andrew Nembhard's inbounds pass to Siakam with 0.9 seconds remaining. Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle was adamant that Martin fouled Siakam on that final play, but judging from the replays, it looked like Martin got all ball before ever making any contact with Siakam.

It obviously would've been nice for Washington to sink at least one of those free throws to avoid that last-second drama, but again, the Mavs keep finding different ways to win. How many times over the past two years have we seen a game like that end in a loss for Dallas?

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks goes to the basket during the first half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

As good (and fun) as the Mavs have been early on, Irving knows his team still has a long way to go to get to the level they want to be at.

"We haven't earned anything in this league yet," Irving said. "We consistently do it every night, and that's how you build your identity in this league and you earn your respect. We try not to put the cart before the horse."

With that being said, though, Mavs fans have earned the right to enjoy this start and, dare I say, dream big again. After two years of nothing but gut punches, a 7-4 start built on a generational teenager, a healthy veteran star and a team that genuinely seems to like playing together is a foundation Mavs fans have been waiting on.

Irving acknowledged the preseason doubt, saying the team heard "a lot of the noise" and chose not to let outside voices into the locker room. If he keeps playing like prime Kyrie, though, and if Flagg keeps rewriting the record books at this current pace, those voices of doubt are going to continue to get a whole lot quieter.

The Mavericks will now hit the road for a big three-game trip that will show just how real this start is, beginning Thursday against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Target Center at 7 p.m. CT. Dallas then visits the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 14 and the Boston Celtics on Nov. 15.

#2693. Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season

EUGENE — One of Oregon football's most important defensive players is done for the season.

Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon's 41-28 win over Ohio State, Dan Lanning announced on Monday.

"Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he's been here," Lanning said. "Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum's done for the year, he had a knee injury, he'll end up having surgery."

Tuioti was among the Ducks' leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front.

In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game.

"I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on," Lanning said. "He left it on the line there on the field, and I don't know if he'll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky."

Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts.

#2691. Views from the Game: Rockets defeat Nuggets 110-100; TDS speaks with Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun

The Houston Rockets faced the Denver Nuggets in unfamiliar territory on Monday. The Rockets entered Monday night's game on their first two-game losing streak of the season after their 102-99 loss to the Phoenix Suns on Saturday.

In that game, the Rockets struggled from the field as the Suns led by double digits in the first quarter. The Rockets eventually got back in the game and even took a six-point lead at one point in the second half. Still, even a fourth-quarter resurgence from Alperen Sengun, who struggled the first three quarters, wasn't enough to keep the Rockets from dropping their second straight game.

The Rockets welcomed the Nuggets, who are coming off a win down in Mexico City over the Los Angeles Clippers. The Rockets have been without Steven Adams and Clint Capela for several games and also added Oscar Tshiebwe to their injury report with an illness. That means the Rockets will be without all three of their backup centers, leaving Sengun as the only active center for Monday's game.

Ime Udoka did mention how both Steven Adams and Clint Capela are targeting the upcoming road trip, specifically the Washington and Miami games, as possible return dates. That would be a welcome sight for a Rockets team that currently ranks 12th in rebounding after being near or at the top every season of Ime Udoka's Rockets tenure.

The Rockets got off to a fast start, led by Durant, who made his first three shots, including one from beyond the arc. Durant was as aggressive in the first quarter as he has been in several games. The quarter was back and forth, as neither team could get much separation.

The Nuggets started to take advantage of the Rockets' lack of depth at center as Jokic went to work once Sengun went to the bench. However, the Rockets put together a good finish to the quarter, and a Tari Eason 3-pointer put them up 32-24 at the end of the first quarter. Durant led all scorers with 11 points in the first 12 minutes.

The Rockets carried that momentum into the second quarter, scoring the first 11 points and building a lead of as much as 19. The Rockets played with much more force and composure than in their first half against the Suns. The Rockets had 13 assists out of their first 20 made baskets. The Rockets maintained the lead, taking a 54-40 lead into halftime.

The third quarter saw the Nuggets cut the lead to under double digits early as they started the quarter on fire from the field. The Rockets, meanwhile, saw their shooting fall off a cliff, starting 2-for-14 from the field as the Nuggets came back from an early 18-point deficit to tie the game at 5:02.

That's when Marcus Smart and Tari Eason entered the game, and the Rockets' defensive intensity immediately rose. The Rockets strung together good defensive possessions that led to easy baskets and pushed the lead back to nine at 71-62. Despite a rough start to the quarter, the Rockets led 77-68 heading into the fourth quarter.

In the fourth quarter, both teams played at a high level for the first time. On one end, Sengun scored in the paint; on the other, Jamal Murray could not miss from mid-range. The Rockets had a slim six-point lead midway through the fourth quarter.

That's when Sengun took over: he not only scored in the paint to give the Rockets a 98-90 lead, but he also assisted on the next two baskets, helping the Rockets put the game away with a 110-100 win. The win snapped the Rockets' first two-game losing streak of the season.

After the game, Ime Udoka, Kevin Durant, and Alperen Sengun spoke to the media. Udoka said the Rockets did a much better job taking care of the basketball and distributing it, and that they finished with 29 assists. SB Nation asked Durant whether it is easier to figure out the defense when he's initiating the offense.

Sengun helped close out the Nuggets with his own great passing and running the pick-and-roll with Durant. Here are both players praising each other's games after last night's win.

The Rockets now begin preparing for their old nemesis, Steph Curry and the Golden State Warriors, who come to town Wednesday with an 8-3 record and have won their last eight games.

#2690. Warriors' surprising turnaround has changed everything about their present - and future

The Golden State Warriors are heading out on their first extended road trip of the season and they're packing a few items that no one would have expected just two weeks ago. An 8-3 record. And a slot in the top four in the Western Conference.

Yeah, it's early. Very early. The season is only 13% complete. There are many ups and downs, stories and challenges ahead. But after an 0-3 start that seemed to confirm the worst of the skeptics' scenarios, the Warriors have transformed into a team that has not only been fun to watch but is creating bright scenarios for the future.

"We're doing all the things we need to convince ourselves we're the team we think we can be," Stephen Curry said recently.

What is the cause of this dramatic change in fortunes and vibe?

Is it the magic in the building, left over from the Valkyries' spectacular playoff run?

Possibly, and I'm not even kidding. Synergy between teams and coworkers is a real thing. Winning teams raise the bar for all the other franchises in their market: sibling teams definitely push each other even more. The Warriors were totally invested in the Valkyries' success, showing up at games, repping their gear, celebrating with them. And the Valkyries reminded the veteran Warriors of all the joy that comes with winning together.

Is it my provocative question to Curry on Warriors media day, when I asked him how it felt that some people don't expect them to even make the playoffs and he said "Damn!" and walked off the podium?

I am kidding about that moment, specifically. But, in general, the Warriors are a very proud group and they were well aware of the lowered expectations surrounding a team that was once only spoken of in terms of championship runs. Starting 0-3 made that negative noise louder.

"It's hard not to hear it," Curry said. "We try not to play into it. We hate losing."

Is the turnaround the result of something that initially looked demoralizing but could end up being a blessing in disguise? The unavailability of Kristaps Porzingis?

Porzingis never even got his season started, has since stepped away from basketball and the Warriors stopped paying his salary. The development has meant that Steve Kerr has gone with a lineup that allows rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to play power forward instead of small forward, a better fit, and also to play Draymond Green at center where he continues to play well. Not waiting around for the theoretical return of Porzingis also means the Warriors know exactly where they stand when February's trade deadline rolls around.

Or is this bounce in the Warriors' play due to just one factor? The new guy?

"Yax," Curry has said, more than once, when asked what's different. Lendeborg, the 11th pick in last June's draft, has been a revelation and has become an instant and integral part of the Bay Area sports landscape. His immediate impact has changed so many negative narratives around the Warriors, such as Kerr doesn't like rookies or general manager Mike Dunleavy doesn't know what he's doing.

"Our second best player is a rookie," Green said Saturday night. "He's only played 10 games."

The Warriors will face heightened competition on this long trip: They start with the Rockets and Spurs, currently two of the top five teams in the West, and also a revenge match against Memphis, which beat the Warriors in their home opener. When they come home Nov. 22, they host the Celtics, one of the top teams in the East.

The Warriors are still just getting started but there's a lot to like right now. The team feels like it's on a different trajectory. Curry is playing at superstar level, averaging 30.6 points a game, and (knock wood) doesn't seem to be hampered by his knee issues. The depth of the team allows Kerr to limit veteran minutes. Lendeborg is making non-Steph minutes survivable.

"My take is we're a very resilient team," Curry said.

The team entered Tuesday ranked second in offensive rating and 11th in defensive rating. On Monday Kerr said, "We have a chance to be, I think, a top-10 offense and defense. And that's what it takes to be a great team in this league, a real contender. And that's our goal."

Also important: the Warriors look like they're having fun again. They seem connected, energized and the chemistry is good. Jimmy Butler's amusing turn as an assistant coach on Monday, sitting on the bench in coaching gear, carrying a clipboard with the instruction "PASS TO STEPH" is one example.

The hope is for Butler to be back in about two months. The Warriors hope to be in a position to make a move at the trade deadline in early February. All of a sudden, not only does the Warriors' future look promising, the present is surprisingly bright.

#2689. Las Vegas Raiders get their gold mined by the 49ers

The Las Vegas Raiders traveled to Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California, to renew the Battle of the Bay rivalry with the San Francisco 49ers. A rivalry that has meant so much to the two fan bases. Turnovers were the story of this contest. When the clock read zero, the Raiders had committed five turnovers and allowed 30+ points on defense for the sixth straight week.

Kirk Cousins had his worst game as the signal caller for the Raiders. In the first half, he only threw the ball eight times. By the end, Cousins threw three interceptions, with one pick-six after recovering his own fumble. Things simply did not go his way today.

Ashton Jeanty regained his starting position and managed 25 yards on six carries. In the passing game where he has made his largest impact, he caught five passes for -5.0 yards. Mike Washington Jr. was subjected to simply awful run blocking, finishing the game with -3.0 yards on six carries with a long of four yards.

Bowers played his first game near his hometown of Napa, California, with reportedly around 50 friends and family in attendance. He would punish the 49ers, finishing with 111 yards on seven catches, including a 21-yard score. A questionable spot robbed him of a second touchdown.

Early on, Raiders defensive playcaller Rob Leonard continued getting his lunch money stolen by an opposing offensive play caller. The 49ers drove down the field on the opening possession in 12 plays, five passes, seven runs and scored. On the second possession, the 49ers ran the ball down the Raiders' throats. Brock Purdy, the 49ers quarterback, would finish the game with 40 yards rushing on seven carries. Including a rushing touchdown which put the 49ers up 14-0.

By the end of the 49ers third drive the Raiders defense surrendered 94 yards rushing, while being on the field for every play except three with 1:52 seconds to play in the first quarter. What we heard from the television broadcasters was that it was 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan's goal to run the ball 40 times against the Raiders' putrid run defense.

After going three-and-out on their first drive, Kirk Cousins gets settled in and hits passes to Jack Bech, Brock Bowers, and Jalen Nailor. Driving the Raiders downfield when the end of the quarter makes them switch sides. Cousins finishes the drive off with his team leading with the second rushing touchdown of the year. Drawing the Raiders to within a score.

Raiders' defense continued to allow nearly six yards per carry to the 49ers offense. On 4th and 1, the run blocking of the 49ers knocked the Raiders' defenders three yards off the line of scrimmage. Raiders followed it up by running some type of zone blitz where both defensive tackles dropped into zone coverage and surrendered a passing touchdown to McCaffrey.

After a Raiders offensive possession netting a field goal, the Raiders were down 21-10 and needed a defensive stop to close out the half. Maxx Crosby would get his fourth sack of the season and a false start penalty would end the half. At the end of the half, the 49ers had ran the ball 25 times for 125 yards and two touchdowns.

First play of the second half, Cousins fumbled the football, picked it up and threw a pick-6, 17 seconds into the second half. Exactly what the Raiders could not afford to have happen. To be fair, everything is resting on his shoulders and in order for the Raiders to have any chance of winning any game, he can't afford to make a mistake.

In the retribution drive after the turnover, Cousins came right back, completing seven of seven throws. finishing with a 21-yard touchdown pass to Bowers to level the score at 28-17. Mistakes happen, but atoning for them is critical. With just under 10 minutes remaining in the 3rd quarter, the 49ers offense would take the field for the first time in the second half.

Treydan Stukes, the Raiders' second-round pick, fooled Purdy, intercepted the pass, tried to fall numerous times with no one around to tackle him and stumbled back to the 30-yard line of the 49ers. Momentum shifts are a huge thing, giving the Raiders an opportunity to get it back to a one-score game. However, in the most self-sabotaging way ever, Cousins nearly threw an interception to a defensive lineman; the very next play, Fred Warner peanut-punches the ball out of Bowers hands and the 49ers recover the ball.

Four plays later, the Raiders get a 4th-and-short stop and a turnover on downs for the first time in a long time. Five turnovers were committed by both teams in the third quarter alone.

On the next drive, Cousins hits Michael Mayer for a nice gain and as he fought to reach the goal line, disaster struck. Mayer was tackled and fell on top of a defender, while another 49ers defender punched the ball out of his hands just before he crossed the goal line. Negating a potential score, turning the ball over yet again, giving the 49ers a touchback.

From there, the 49ers would drive past midfield with a few runs. But the lack of a Raiders pass rush gave Purdy enough time to find Jordan Watkins open for a 37-yard touchdown catch.

On the ensuing possession, the Raiders drove to the goal line again, behind a 33-yard catch-and-run from Bowers that appeared to stretch the ball over the pylon but was ruled out of bounds. Cousins' quarterback sneak was stuffed when Warner leaped over the pile after the snap. On the next play, Mayer was called for offensive pass interference, negating his own touchdown catch. Followed up with Cousins' second interception of the game, the second turnover inside the red zone, turnover number four and the third straight turnover.

But the hits just kept on coming; in junk time, Cousins would throw his third interception of the day, fourth straight turnover and fifth total. Cousins had Tre Tucker open deep, loaded up, putting his full body into the throw, only for it to fall short and into the waiting arms of a 49ers defender, mercifully allowing this game to come to an end.

#2688. Nets' Julius Randle doesn't believe team is 'letting go of the rope'

Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle has maintained that the Nets have to work on being more connected as a team when they're facing adversity, especially given that they're 2-8 through their first 10 games. Brooklyn is currently 0-2 on its four-game road trip and while the Nets understand that there are 72 more games to go, Randle is giving his take on where the team stands now.

"Honestly, I'm not really sure. I gotta watch the film, to be honest. But, they were getting a lot of stuff off of switching, and credit to them," Randle said to the media after Sunday's 130-93 loss to the Dallas Mavericks. Brooklyn were within striking distance throughout the first quarter, but the Mavericks built as much as a 26-point lead in the second quarter as the Nets looked discouraged by the growing deficit.

"[We] just got to find a way to get back to being a connected group on both ends. I feel like we do a good job of communicating, but it's not really translating," Randle said when asked for his takeaways from this weekend. "So, [we have to figure out] how to make things translate. Basketball is a funny game; it can turn really quick. So, I think [we have to] continue to be optimistic, stay positive."

This hasn't been the first time that Randle or any of the other players have had to address the team being disconnected and it's easy to see when it comes to the numerous defensive breakdowns. For his part, Randle ended Sunday's loss to the Mavericks with 13 points, four rebounds, and four assists, but he was also a -33 plus/minus, easily the worst mark on the team.

As head coach Jordi Fernandez and center Mo Wagner have spoken on since Sunday's game ended, the Nets eventually have to find a way to get on the same page if they're going to string together some wins. Wednesday's contest pits them against the New Orleans Pelicans (4-7) and if Brooklyn isn't careful, they could find themselves with an 0-3 record on their current road trip.

#2687. What We Learned from the Spurs win over the Suns

It's hard not to feel like you're watching a mirage during some of these games. The level of play is excellent and the bits and pieces you might be tempted to pick at are scarce. The wins are piling up. The vibes are good. Everything is going according to plan. Nothing to see here…right?

Right! Look, I'm not going to even try to play devil's advocate here. No one wants to be the guy pointing at the Alien dropping 40 and 11 over 25 minutes and saying, "actually, this is bad." If that's a take you'd like to read then I can assure the internet is full of people willing to take you up on the offer. For my part, and if you've come to this website today, I'm assuring you, I genuinely find it hard to think of a less interesting angle to come at this from.

Victor Wembanyama is simply brilliant. He's been brilliant, he's brilliant now, and he only seems to be getting more brillianter as we go along. Twelve of his fifteen made shots on Monday were dunks or layups, and nine of those were dunks. Four different teammates threw him an alley-oop. The Spurs are running a dizzying array of different motions that all end up at the same destination, which is a Wembanyama dunk. The threes, instead of feeling like something he has to do to open up the lane, now just arrive in the natural rhythm of the game. He made two threes all night, a digestif tacked on at the end of a satisfying meal.

Vic even hit a Dream Shake in the middle of the 2nd quarter that left me staring off in the distance in disbelief.

I sometimes try to avoid writing about the Victor Wembanyama of it all when I do these because it feels too easy. What did we learn from the Spurs win? They still have the best player on the planet and he helps a lot. Case closed. To his credit, he goes out of his way to make ignoring him next to impossible.

The problem, if there is one, is that regular season basketball does actually seem easy for him at this point. That's not a mirage. I have no doubt about how hard he's worked to achieve the level he's currently operating on, but that doesn't change the fact that watching him dismantle the average NBA team every other night doesn't look very challenging. He's like Will Hunting ranting at Professor Lambeau about how easy it is to solve those supposedly impossible graph theory equations.

Victor's ascension this season is impressive, and I want to do my best to appreciate the casual brilliance we are privy to on a regular basis, but that greatness comes at a cost, and that cost is a raised ceiling. I simply don't care that he can drop 50 on the Mavs or 40 on the Suns. I don't care that he can snuff out the Blazers. I'm sure there will be another jaw-dropping stat line on Wednesday when he plays the Bulls, and I'm sure it will be met with another polite nod from me.

None of this is his fault, mind you. The schedule is the schedule and the teams are the teams. He's taking care of business, and that's all you can really ask of him.

I guess I've just spent the last nine games of this winning streak telling myself I still don't know what I'm looking at and I really believe anyone who tells you they do is lying. The ease with which they are winning these games is real. Every conclusion we draw from it…well, that's a little more hazy. I try to grab on to things I know. "The Spurs are Good." "The Suns are Bad." "Wemby is Tall," and project out from there but I end up feeling like I'm chasing the ghost of a conclusion. The idea of a resolution instead of an actual one.

This is a champagne problem at most. Like, what, I'm having a bad time because I can't tell if the Spurs are great, really great, or generationally amazing? A few years ago we were sitting through a sixteen-game losing streak and then an eighteen-game one, on our way to the lottery again and again. Now I'm hemming and hawing because our first brush with success last spring has got me feeling antsy.

The thing I'm dancing around here is that the Finals loss is an albatross around our necks that we're just going to have to wear. There's no two ways about it. I'm encouraged by the things I'm seeing from this new three-guard- Hydra, but I won't feel comfortable until I know it can outscore Jalen Brunson when he's going Nuclear. I love that Victor seems more calm and assured in his decision making, but I still have nightmares about KAT finding a way to neutralize him. Every time we race out to a lead this season, my brain remembers the blown leads in June.

The context of the past clouds everything from the present and I don't think there's an easy fix for that feeling. It shouldn't sully our enjoyment of the current moment, but it does ground the results in a certain reality.

All of this is certainly real enough, but none of it really matters.

I don't feel qualified to talk about what Dylan Harper is doing. It's a level of basketball that I recognize as great but have difficulty quantifying, because my analysis tends to err on the side of "oh my God, how did he do that?" Nuance exits the room when he has the ball in his hands. There is a grace and fluidity to his game that is hypnotic, whether he's getting to the basket with relative ease or casually spinning into a midrange jumper. I don't know how to say this as a compliment, but it's fascinatingly boring to watch. He's operating at breakneck speed but still in complete control, sort of like how F1 cars can look a little blah during a race until you blink and realize they're going like 200 mph.

The caveat with Dylan is, obviously, his youth. It's simultaneously the most exciting and frustrating thing about him. That control I just alluded to can prove elusive sometimes. Sometimes he seems almost like he's just watching the game happen to him and forgets that he's more than capable of grabbing the reins. He started the game last night a little bit adrift. Whether that's a byproduct of the three-guard lineup's growing pains or him simply sitting back and watching Wemby cook like the rest of us, he was kind of invisible, and a guy like Harper just shouldn't be invisible. After the game, Mitch talked about calling him out specifically during a timeout in the 3rd, and that wake-up call seemed to snap him back into place. He absolutely torched the Suns in that 3rd quarter, going 6-of-8 from the field and effectively putting the game out of reach after Phoenix briefly tried to make a run. He is, without a doubt, the 2nd best player on the team from a talent perspective, and that this already kinda feels indisputable is the most shocking thing of all.

It would've been so easy to just write off De'Aaron Fox this season, as evidenced by that fact that so many people did, in fact, write him off. But he's been really fun to watch so far this year. I love the way he fits into the similar but different skill sets of our guards, and he seems a little more freed up now that Harper and Castle can take on more responsibility. He's still so fast and he still has great vision, and last night he finished with 15 points, six assists and nine rebounds. His chemistry with Wembanyama has only gotten better, with four of those six assists going to Wemby, and their propensity for lobs and oops of all types seems to have rubbed off on everyone around them. It's kind of exactly what you would want from a veteran leader in the starting lineup. Everyone else is right though, the Spurs probably should've just shipped him last summer because everyone on Twitter was mad.

Are you ever going to stop having an existential crisis about the Spurs this season?

Are you kidding? My entire brand is "existential crisis about the Spurs." What would I even write about if not that?

You could analyze the gameplay? Trending stats? Maybe break down different plays the offense runs? Talk about defensive schemes?

You sound insane right now. Completely bonkers.

I just think people come here trying to figure out what they learned from the game and you're only even talking about the journey through the dark night of the soul you went through on a random Monday. We're eleven games into the season! You don't want to, like, build to that?

Shooters shoot. I'm not going to lie to the readers about the fact that I can't sit still and watch Wembanyama dunk on dudes without stressing about the inexorable march of time or whatever.

I'm not asking you to lie, but also, like, can you not sit still and just watch Wembanyama dunk on dudes without stressing about the inexorable march of time or whatever? Like, are you incapable of doing that?

#2686. Does 49ers trade for Keenan Allen solidify their Super Bowl hopes?

The San Francisco 49ers acquired veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick just hours before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10.

It's no secret around the NFL that the Niners have a shortage of available wideouts, making the addition of Allen all the more vital to San Francisco's passing game.

The 49ers have been dealt injuries throughout the season Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr., De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson and Christian Kirk. Each week, there has been someone in the Niners' WR room who steps up to the mantle. Now, Allen gets his turn as San Francisco found their plug-in at receiver.

He returns to the Bay Area having played his collegiate years at Cal from 2010 to 2012. From Cal, he was selected by San Diego Chargers with the 76th overall pick in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft. Allen was runner-up for Offensive Rookie of the Year but he developed into the Chargers' No. 1-receiver. He would become a six-time Pro Bowl selection in 10 seasons, even as the team moved to Los Angeles.

He spent a season with the Chicago Bears in 2024, then returned to LA for another season with the Chargers. He signed with Indianapolis during the offseason.

With Allen back on the West Coast, the hope is to earn the league's most prized piece of jewelry.

Does Allen have enough left in the tank to help bring a Super Bowl to the Bay Area?

Allen comes to San Francisco as a 34-year-old veteran receiver in his 14th NFL season, which bears the question of if he has enough in the tank to be a contributing piece to the 49ers offense. Allen is added to a star-studded wide receiver room, but still, looming injuries loom are a cause of concern, at least until guys start trending upward.

He'll likely come in as a starter. Allen is known for his elite route-running, high IQ and superb ball-tracking and catching ability. Nothing thrown Allen's way gets dropped.

Allen caught 40 balls for 351 yards and 1 touchdown in eight games with the Colts during the 2026 NFL season. He's shared 22% of targets and has a nearly 69% catch rating. He averages 8.8 yards per catch.

His addition provides Brock Purdy with another weapon to find trust in, especially while the San Francisco receiver room slowly gets healthy. Adding Allen means the team doesn't necessarily have to rush guys back to the field.

Plus, Jordan Watkins is coming off a week where he caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown. He continues to improve. Having a threat like Allen alongside Watkins will likely open things up for himself.

The 49ers are still the favorite to win the Super Bowl with +550 odds, according to BetMGM, currently tied with the Buffalo Bills.

For San Francisco, the team's hopes will ride on health and availability. Allen isn't a young buck anymore at 34. Example A, Evans is 33 years old and look how much time he's missed.

No question at what the 49ers will get from the vets on the field, it's a matter of getting them on the field at 100%. Allen has been relatively healthy in 2026 and that's good news for San Francisco.

Allen appeared in every game, except one, for the Colts having missed Week 4 with a groin injury. Since then, he's been dependable, especially production wise. Maybe not the fantasy pickup he once was, but Allen does the things that contributes to winning football games.

MADISON – Wisconsin men's basketball faces a team Nov. 10 that won 21 games last year. There's a big catch, though.

Most of Fairfield's wins were against Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference competition. The Stags' 21-13 season ended with a loss to Siena, an eventual NCAA Tournament No. 16 seed, in the MAAC semifinals.

Fairfield (1-1) is visiting the Kohl Center tonight for the second all-time meeting against the Badgers (2-0). (The first meeting was in 1992, when Michael Finley's 24 points and nine rebounds led the Badgers to a 76-55 win at the UW Field House.)

#2683. Today's top games to watch, best bets, odds: Rays vs. Yankees, Penguins vs. Capitals and more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The last time the Tampa Bay Rays reached the American League Championship Series, they needed five games to get past the New York Yankees in the AL Division Series. They're hoping to make it a little easier on themselves this time around.

Make your MLB picks using the BetMGM bonus code CBSSPORTS and get up to $1,500 in bonus bets if your first bet loses:

Tampa Bay attempts to complete a sweep of the 2026 ALDS when they square off against New York at 8 p.m. ET in Game 3 on Wednesday at Yankee Stadium. The Rays, who defeated the Yankees in this round in 2020 en route to the second World Series appearance in franchise history, edged New York 1-0 in this year's series opener before pushing their AL East rivals to the brink of elimination with a 5-2 victory in Game 2.

The Rays went 7-6 against New York during the regular season but lost four of the six contests at Yankee Stadium, including three of four in their penultimate series of the campaign. Tampa Bay was outscored 15-6 in its final two games in the Bronx, but its pitching staff has kept the Yankees in check thus far in the ALDS.

New York was limited to one hit in Game 1 as Drew Rasmussen had a no-hitter for 7 2/3 innings before Austin Wells ripped a double down the right field line. However, Wells made an ill-advised decision to try and stretch it into a triple and was thrown out easily at third base. Rays closer Bryan Baker worked a perfect ninth to preserve the win.

The Yankees didn't fare much better offensively in Game 2 as they registered just four hits, two of which were solo homers by Ben Rice. They were even worse defensively, committing four errors -- including three in the first inning that helped give Tampa Bay a 1-0 lead.

Tampa Bay will look to punch its ticket to the ALCS behind Nick Martinez, who set a career high with 15 wins this year and matched another with a 3.10 ERA. The 36-year-old right-hander posted a better ERA on the road (2.38) than at home (3.90) during the regular season and had a 2.16 mark in two turns at Yankee Stadium. Martinez held New York to one run over six innings in a no-decision on May 22 and gave up just two while recording a season-high seven strikeouts across six frames in a 2-0 loss on Sept. 22.

The Yankees are counting on Max Fried to help extend their postseason. The 32-year-old left-hander, who allowed just one run and three hits over six innings against the Boston Red Sox in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series for his first win in 10 total starts at Yankee Stadium in 2026, was tagged for four runs and six hits across 6 2/3 frames as he took the loss in his lone home outing against the Rays.

Two NL Division Series take place Wednesday evening, including Game 4 of the matchup between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Atlanta Braves at 6 p.m. ET at Truist Park. The two-time reigning world champion Dodgers are one win away from their third straight trip to the NLCS after defeating the Braves 3-1 on Tuesday.

The other NLDS resumes at 10 p.m. ET, when the San Diego Padres host the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 at Petco Park. San Diego lost a pair of one-run heartbreakers in Milwaukee before staying alive with Tuesday's 4-3 home triumph that was closed out by Michael King, who kept the Brewers off the board over the final two innings after permitting only one run over five frames in his Game 2 start just two days earlier.

Two teams seeking a third consecutive victory collide at the Honda Center as the Anaheim Ducks (2-0-0) host the Edmonton Oilers (2-0-1) at 10 p.m. ET. #2682. Week 10 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Corey Kiner, Tank Dell among top pickups

Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

With Kirk Cousins heading back to Minnesota, the Raiders can finally put their first-overall pick under center. While you're not going to want to use Mendoza against the Seahawks defense this week, his outlook for the rest of the season is quite promising as a highly-drafted pick attached to Klint Kubiak.

The Heisman Trophy winner proved himself to be a good leader in college with excellent on-field awareness and the toughness needed to overcome adversity during games. He has a strong arm to make any throw, but it's his touch passing that stood out. Though Mendoza's not fast enough to be a meaningful runner in the pros, he has enough speed to scramble his way out of trouble and pick up yards on the ground. This all amounts to an intriguing fantasy QB2 with room to grow.

The quarterback position is very picked over at the moment. Malik Willis was featured in this spot last week, but he's now playing through a groin injury that's limited his abilities as a runner and neutered his fantasy potential. So, all that's left are uncomfortable streaming options.

The Steelers are coming off their bye week, which should help the 42-year-old Rodgers (turns 43 in December) feel refreshed for a date with the division rival Bengals.

Rodgers hasn't had many favorable opponents this season, but he did take advantage of his easiest matchup. That just happened to be against the Bengals in Week 3, when the veteran passed for 292 yards and three touchdowns en route to a QB8 finish.

In his last visit to Cincinnati, Rodgers threw four touchdowns back in Week 7 of the 2025 campaign. He's not a slam-dunk streamer, but he's a solid one given the options this week.

Desperation streaming options (if healthy)

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

The elite backup RBs who are one injury away from stardom should be rostered everywhere and I'll continue to highlight them in this space until they no longer qualify for this article.

It was clear early in the season that Johnson was one of the best backups to roster, in case anything ever happens to Kenneth Walker III. In recent weeks, Johnson's value has increased even more now that he's offering weekly flex production.

The rookie posted a fluky 128 receiving yards and a score in Week 8, but he followed it up with 34 yards and another touchdown on Sunday. Upcoming matchups with the Falcons, Cardinals and Bills are all spots where Johnson could be a viable flex play while also offering league-winning upside if Walker ever misses time.

Black is in the same situation as Johnson; you can basically just swap Walker's name with Christian McCaffrey's in the previous section.

The 49ers' rookie plays in one of the best offenses in the league and has flashed his potential with at least 60 rushing yards in three of his first eight games, while serving as CMC's direct backup. That includes the past two games, when Black turned 12 touches into 63 yards and a TD against the Falcons, as well as Sunday's outing, which resulted in 11 carries for a season-high 70 yards.

Next up is the Cowboys defense, which is a top-five matchup for fantasy running backs. The 49ers are 4-point favorites in a game with the highest projected point total in Week 10 at 55.5.

Stashing a talented No. 2 back playing behind a 30-year-old starter who handled 450 touches last year is just an obvious move. Black should be rostered everywhere as a flex option with RB1 upside if McCaffrey were ever sidelined.

Rhamondre Stevenson left Sunday's game with a knee injury and was very quickly ruled out. Mike Vrabel didn't have an update Monday morning, but did acknowledge that his back was undergoing an MRI. With TreVeyon Henderson already sidelined indefinitely, that leaves Kiner as the next man up.

Though Kiner hasn't been asked to do much as a pass-catcher, the 2025 UDFA has shown some juice in the run game by topping 50 yards in three of his last five outings in a change-of-pace role.

If Stevenson can't suit up in Week 10, which seems unlikely due to news that he'll probably miss some time, Kiner immediately becomes a high-end fantasy RB3 with the usual touchdown upside that comes with a starter's workload. We can't lock that outcome in, though until we get a proper update on Stevenson's injury.

Josh Jacobs fractured his finger and is set to undergo surgery that will keep him out a maximum of three games.

MarShawn Lloyd missed Week 9 due to a knee injury, which allowed Johnson to step up in Jacobs' absence. Johnson finished with 68 yards and a touchdown, making him the RB11 on the week with just MNF left to be played.

If you're wondering why Johnson isn't higher on this list, just take a look at Green Bay's upcoming schedule. The Packers face the Vikings this week, then have a bye before taking on the Rams.

So, even with Jacobs sidelined, this isn't the ideal setup for a spot starter. On top of that, we aren't sure if/when Lloyd will be available. If Lloyd is active in Week 10, it only further muddies the projections.

If Lloyd remains out, Johnson would be a risky RB3/flex versus the Vikings. If Lloyd plays, then both players would be risky flex options.

With the Saints cutting Kendre Miller, Estimé stepped into a significant role in his first game since joining the Saints. The result was a 47% snap share, which led to 15 carries for 72 yards and a touchdown, as well as another five yards on a catch.

Estimé's presence helped kickstart New Orleans' rushing attack, but his fantasy outlook is directly tied to Travis Etienne Jr.'s health. Etienne, who can be activated off IR at any time, wasn't ready to practice last week. Once we see him back on the field, it will severely diminish Estimé's fantasy value.

However, if Etienne misses another week, fantasy managers will be able to start Estimé as a fringe low-end RB2.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. at TEN (33% rostered)

Sione Vaki vs. NE (Germany) (2% rostered)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

DeMario Douglas has always been a risky receiver to put in your fantasy lineup due to his low floor. We witnessed that occur in Week 7, when he only delivered three catches for 23 yards.

However, Douglas has posted at least 12 fantasy points in his other four outings over the last five weeks, finishing as a top-10 WR three times. After hauling in five of his nine targets for 102 yards in Week 9, he currently sits as the WR23 with just Monday Night Football remaining.

Four touchdowns during this stretch have helped his cause, but he's come away with very respectable yardage totals in these games with at least 65 in each.

A.J. Brown's recovery timeline remains uncertain and with a bye looming, it seems likely we won't see him until Week 12 at the earliest. Fantasy managers can continue to take advantage by starting Douglas as a WR3/flex option with temporary upside.

Dell's return from a near career-ending injury is one of the best stories in the NFL this season. The fact that he's been productive since getting back on the field only makes it more incredible.

While his 43-yard catch on one target in Week 7 was a bit fluky, it's hard to ignore a nine-target outing this past week. Dell finished the day with four grabs, 105 yards and a score and looked good in the process. However, he still only ran 50% of the routes in a Houston passing attack that's known for rotating receivers behind Nico Collins. We'll need to see more from Dell before we can trust him as an every-week fantasy starter, but he's done enough to warrant being added in most formats as a potential boom-or-bust WR3/flex.

After back-to-back games with at least 50 yards, it was discouraging to see Williams underwhelm with just three catches for 25 yards this week. I'm still holding out hope though.

The rookie continues to play the most snaps and run the most routes in the Commanders' receiver room. This was the third straight outing where Williams accomplished that feat, following Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury.

It's possible Williams levels off as a low-ceiling WR4/flex option for fantasy, but I'm holding for at least another week. The talent is evident and Washington has one of the top-10 easiest schedules for fantasy receivers the rest of the way.

Douglas has played four games this year that weren't impacted by injury. In those contests, the rookie has posted stat lines of 5-94-0, 2-70-2, 4-43-0 and 6-70-0.

With Malik Willis heading to IR, Douglas's fantasy ceiling takes a hit. However, he's still an intriguing rookie who is emerging as the No. 1 target in his offense.

When a first-year player is showing this kind of production early in his career, it's worth taking notice. Even with Kyle McCord under center, Douglas can be started as a WR4/flex given his intriguing matchups against the Colts and Bills the next two weeks.

It's easy to forget, but Bryant had a growing role in the Broncos' passing attack during the opening month before being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. In those first four games, Bryant topped 40 yards three times.

So, it was great to see him post a season-high 56 yards and a touchdown on four catches in his first game back since the injury. Jaylen Waddle also suffered a concussion, but he should be cleared after their Week 10 bye.

Regardless, Bryant was a borderline flex option early in the season and has returned with an even better performance. Given Waddle's struggles and Courtland Sutton's age, there's a non-zero chance Bryant becomes the most valuable fantasy receiver in Denver for the rest of the season.

Watkins' fantasy value is difficult to assess because it's entirely dependent on the health of the other receivers in San Francisco.

Keenan Allen was acquired at the trade deadline, but most of the other wideouts on the roster are injured. Deebo Samuel Sr. is nearing a return from a hamstring injury that kept him out for the last month. Mike Evans' Achilles tendinitis is an ongoing problem with no clear recovery timeline. I'll be surprised if he suits up in Week 10. Demarcus Robinson is apparently playing at less than 100%, while De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are on IR.

That opened the door for Watkins, who put up four receptions, 86 yards and a touchdown versus the Raiders. That's his second consecutive quality stat line, after a 56-yard performance versus the Falcons prior to the Niners' Week 8 bye.

If everything remains the same with Evans and Deebo sitting out, Watkins will be a boom-or-bust WR4/flex option in a good matchup with the Cowboys this week. However, once Allen is up to speed and the other receivers are healthy, Watkins won't be worth rostering in redraft leagues.

Jordyn Tyson is 54% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Makai Lemon is 53% rostered but would be the No. 3 WR add behind Tyson and D.Douglas, if available.

Courtland Sutton is 53% rostered but would be the No. 6 WR add behind Tyson, D. Douglas, Lemon, C. Douglas and Dell, if available.

Khalil Shakir is 53% rostered but would be the No. 9 WR add behind Tyson, D. Douglas, Lemon, C. Douglas, Dell, Williams, Sutton and Bryant, if available.

Mack Hollins vs. DET (Germany) (5% rostered)

Efton Chism III vs. DET (Germany) (2% rostered)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

In the four games since Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury, Okonkwo has posted stat lines for 4-60-0, 7-69-0, 2-32-0 and 6-57-0.

While he hasn't found the end zone, that type of volume (at least six targets in three of the four appearances) makes him the 10th-most targeted tight end on a per game basis during that stretch.

Okonkwo has moved into the high-end TE2 streamer conversation, with a chance to crack the low-end TE1 range moving forward.

Puka Nacua is heading to IR, Davante Adams is already there and Terrance Ferguson isn't expected back for another couple weeks.

Higbee has disappeared from fantasy relevance following his impressive three-game stretch from Week 3 to Week 5, when he posted 8-62-1, 5-67-0 and 5-83-0. Since then, the veteran has been held to 22 yards or less in four straight contests and hasn't found the end zone.

However, the Rams will have no choice but to increase his targets with Nacua out. That puts Higbee back in the mix as a TE2 streamer with upside.

Eddy Pineiro is 54% rostered but would be the No. 1 K add, if available.

Tyler Bass is 57% rostered but would be the No. 2 K add behind Pinerio, if available.

Quarterbacks: Lamar Jackson, Kyler Murray, Justin Herbert

Running Backs: J.K. Dobbins, Emanuel Wilson

Wide Receivers: Michael Wilson, Xavier Worthy, Chris Godwin Jr., Marvin Harrison Jr., Devaughn Vele

Lamar Jackson is undergoing surgery that will sideline him for 6-10 weeks. If you're stashing him in hopes that he'll return for the fantasy playoffs, you're wasting a roster spot.

Despite the Texans making a trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., he's just part of a big rotation of receivers behind Nico Collins. #2678. Michigan football donors question Kyle Whittingham's future: Report

There has been turmoil in Ann Arbor this past week, with fans questioning the viability of Kyle Whittingham's tenure -- his press conference sound bites not helping -- and made the worse by Michigan football's loss to Michigan State on Saturday.

After the game, Whittingham staunchly said that he would not make any decisions on offensive coordinator Jason Beck until after the season. However, Beck was summarily fired on Sunday, and Whittingham insisted on Monday that it was his decision after watching game film from Saturday's loss.

However, as On3's Pete Nakos tells it, that sounds a little suspicious compared to what he had been hearing.

Nakos appeared on Crain & Cone on Monday, and he said that no decision on Beck had been made as late as 2 p.m. EST (he was fired near 5 p.m. EST), and it didn't appear that there was any plan to oust Beck by Whittingham at any point.

"I admittedly did check in with some folks around like noon, 1 (p.m.) central yesterday, and the decision had not been made," Nakos said. "And it almost came across that he wasn't planning on making any staffing changes at that point. So Kyle Whittingham comes out this morning, said he made the decision. I did check in, though, midday yesterday before that news came down. There was no plan. So, you know, continue to have conversations, try to find out more about how things conspired."

There have been rumors that the call has come from above Whittingham's head, with athletic director Warde Manuel getting involved, but nothing on the record at this point.

But more than that, Nakos reports that high-level donors and the board of regents are now questioning Whittingham's viability after the loss, given that this team is now 5-4 and hasn't consistently looked up to par.

"The other thing I heard Sunday morning was that I think Saturday night, that loss to Michigan State, as painful as it was for Cone, was also an eye-opener for a lot of donors and some board of trustees to say, 'Oh, like this is where we're at, where we just lost to Michigan State at home,'" Nakos said. "You know, I think playing Indiana tight and trying to find some rhythm against Rutgers, that's kind of like, OK, maybe we're turning the corner, and then you basically go scoreless against one of your archrivals."

Of course, Michigan has a lame duck athletic director in Manuel, who will be stepping down at the end of the year. The Wolverines announced that they have started the search for his replacement, and there are indications that it's escalating.

Nakos says that if Michigan hurriedly gets a new AD, the gears could potentially turn on a decision on Whittingham, one way or the other, sooner than many might think. A new AD doesn't guarantee that the former Utah coach would be out, but it would certainly give the school some clarity.

"Well, I mean, they've started the search, so hypothetically, the new president could make this hire by the end of the month and get the new AD in there immediately," Nakos said. "How that all shakes out, I mean, I know that they're in the early process. But Florida State just hired an athletic director basically in 14 days."

#2677. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2673. Tiger Woods 'feeling better' after car crash and arrest before Hero World Challenge, unclear if he will play in Bahamas

Tiger Woods will be on the golf course in the Bahamas next month regardless. Whether he tees it up at the Hero World Challenge, though, is still a mystery.

Woods, who hasn't played competitive golf since the TGL Final days before his crash and arrest in Florida, told Sirius XM PGA Tour Radio on Tuesday that he's "feeling better" and has been "training quite a bit."

While nothing is official and he's not announced any plans, that's undoubtedly a good sign for the 50-year-old with the new PGA Tour season just a few months out.

"I'm feeling better, there's no doubt about that," Woods said. "I've been training quite a bit."

"I will be at Hero," he added with a laugh. "I'm there either way, so I'll see you there."

Woods has hosted the Hero World Challenge, an unofficial Tour event, for years now in the Bahamas. The no-cut tournament has just a 20-man field, and still has three spots open. If Woods wants to play again, that'd be a very easy spot to return.

Woods appeared in a TGL match last season in March, but he was involved in a rollover crash just days later in Jupiter Island, Florida. He was preparing to return for the Masters the next month, but ended up pleading guilty to misdemeanor charges of reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test after his arrest. His driver's license was suspended for five years as a result, too.

Woods hasn't played anywhere since, and has only made a handful of public appearances. He stepped away from the sport and reportedly sought treatment in Switzerland, too.

It's unclear when Woods will play again. He is reportedly expected to compete in the new TGL season in December, though indoor golf is very different from the real thing, especially from a physical standpoint.

Woods ruptured his Achilles and underwent back surgery in 2025, and missed all four major championships that season as a result. The 50-year-old has only played a full tournament in three of his last 11 starts, and has otherwise missed the cut or withdrawn. He last played on the PGA Tour at the British Open in 2024.

There are a few other options for Woods to make his Tour return, if it's not at the Hero World Challenge. He could play alongside his son, Charlie, at the PNC Championship — a 36-hole parent-child event that would allow him to use a cart. He could wait until the Genesis Invitational next season in Los Angeles, too. Woods hosts that event on the Tour each season, and it would be an easy starting point before the major championships get going.

Regardless of what he ends up doing, Woods appears to be in a much better spot now than he was just a few months ago. A return to the sport appears imminent.
